root_cause_label: Staircase logic never correctly raises adjacent tile level to 7 before stepping onto gold at level 8; agent repeatedly misattributes game non-completion to environment/timeout rather than its own flawed build logic
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent writes a series of solution.js implementations that all fail to correctly build a staircase (dropping blocks to raise the current tile level to 7 adjacent to gold), and instead of diagnosing its own algorithmic errors it repeatedly blames environmental timeouts, ending on a trivially wrong direction-cycling stub that cannot win.
t_err_evidence: solution.js created with invalid cell.x/cell.y API fields and undefined 'state' variable in buildStaircase
t_commit_evidence: From step 5 onward every solution is built on the same wrong premise (staircase = drop once adjacent to gold, check gold cell's level rather than building up the current tile). No subsequent step corrects this fundamental error; the agent oscillates between increasingly stripped-down variants but never implements correct incremental-drop logic. With m=34 and all rewrites sharing the same core flaw, failure is locked in at step 5.
t_surface_evidence: node test_runner.js produces only 'DEBUG: invoking game.run(3)' with no trial results, indicating a hang
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks correct understanding of the staircase mechanic: the player must stand on a tile adjacent to gold (level 8) and repeatedly drop blocks to raise THAT TILE's level to 7, then step across the 1-level gap onto gold. Instead the agent drops once, checks the gold cell's level (which is fixed at 8), and incorrectly concludes no further drops are needed. It also misreads the API, assuming cell.x/cell.y exist when the game only provides neighbor type/level via cell.left/up/right/down.
